ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
1000 litres of water is passed through the water system as shown, into two identical tanks. At each junction the water separates into two equal amounts. How many litres of water end up in Tank Y?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: 1000 litres of water is passed through the water system as shown, into two identical tanks. At each junction the water separates into two equal amounts. How many litres of water end up in Tank Y?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a water inlet entered from an arrow above, and the pipe goes downward to a fork. After the fork, one branch leads to the right and finally enters the water tank labeled Y; the other branch leads to the left, and below it another fork appears, of which one outlet enters the water tank labeled X, and the other inner/central outlet enters the water tank labeled Y. Reasoning: The total amount of water is 1000 liters. The problem states that each junction divides the incoming water equally into two portions. The first fork divides 1000 liters into two portions, so 500 liters goes along the right branch directly into Tank Y, and 500 liters goes along the left branch. After the left branch reaches the second fork, it is again equally divided into two portions, so 250 liters of it enters Tank X, and the other 250 liters enters Tank Y through the central outlet. Therefore the total amount of water entering Tank Y is 500 + 250 = 750 liters.

raw_record.question_text: 1000 litres of water is passed through the water system as shown, into two identical tanks. At each junction the water separates into two equal amounts. How many litres of water end up in Tank Y?

method.method_draft: Trace the flow along the pipe network. From the image, the top inlet first reaches a junction where the water splits into a left branch and a right branch. The right branch goes directly down into Tank Y. The left branch continues to another junction, where it splits again: one outlet goes into Tank X and the other inner/central outlet goes into Tank Y. From the text, start with 1000 litres and use the stated rule that every junction divides the incoming water equally. Thus the first split sends 500 litres right to Y and 500 litres left; the second split sends half of the left 500, i.e. 250 litres, to Y. Add the two contributions to Tank Y: 500 + 250 = 750 litres.
